dimensions.name: alpha
dimensions.meaning: L2 penalty on the weights; values are log-spaced

dimensions.name: batch_size
dimensions.meaning: samples per Adam update; values are log-spaced

dimensions.name: depth
dimensions.meaning: number of hidden layers, all of equal width

dimensions.name: learning_rate_init
dimensions.meaning: initial Adam step size; values are log-spaced

dimensions.name: width
dimensions.meaning: neurons per hidden layer; values are log-spaced

beliefs.note: For small datasets (~1k records), moderate depth (2) and width (~100) typically balance capacity and overfitting better than very shallow or very deep/wide nets.
Adam typically performs well with initial learning rates in the 1e-3 to 5e-3 range for standard classification tasks.
Small to moderate L2 regularization is usually beneficial for small datasets to prevent overfitting, but too much hurts performance.
Larger batch sizes often provide more stable gradients, but for small datasets, very large batches may not offer significant gains and can hurt generalization.

trust.notes: General MLP tuning heuristics applied to a small, balanced credit application dataset. Specific optimal values may vary based on feature scaling and data distribution.
